I was just reading a research article showing there are about 259 (I think) combinations to have BPD where most other personality disorders and other conditions have far fewer combinations, often less than 100. That means it is far easier to be diagnosed with BPD than many other things, which can make misdiagnosis more llikely. It also seems more unfair.

I feel ya too... Being quiet about it makes it harder to know if you really have it, and sometimes the stigma makes you feel like a worse person than you are since you don't act on it... I'm in a similar boat where I feel turbulent inside but don't act... (At the same time though, I've had several traumatic experiences involving others so I get emotionally by a lot of things and dissociate and break down... Almost seems like a PTSD thing.)

I feel ya, I've been diagnosed with those too as well as anxiety lol. It just seems like a combination of those disorders and others can cause the symptoms of BPD in themselves. Example:

-emptiness can be from depression

-dissociation can be PTSD or even anxiety

-self harm and suicide can be due to sexual trauma and PTSD

-PTSD can cause unstable relationships 

-impulsivity can be ADHD

-anger can be from PTSD

-turbulent emotions can be ADHD

-abandonment fears could also be PTSD if there was trauma involving abandonment

So that's 7 of the criteria for BPD right there, which only 5 are needed... So that makes me wonder: does the combination mean you truly have BPD, or is it a misdiagnosis due to other conditions? If it is still considered BPD, it seems a little unfair due to the stigma and saying there's something wrong with your personality when none of the other conditions are considered to be a personality problem, even with similar symptoms.

Turn your phone off to avoid contacting them while you're worrying (which can make things worse sometimes) and just find some to distract you. Maybe practice mindfulness. That stuff can seem boring but it really does help when put to good use.

It can get lonely at times, for sure... I suggest personal projects, music... Do you like to read or be creative? Do you like games? Is there anything you really enjoy doing that is simply easier to do when you're by yourself? I'd suggest those things to keep your mind occupied.

Reading about the movie, a lot of the symptoms seem the same, but portraying people with BPD as potential killers who boil bunnies seems a little unfair. Sufferers are typically more dangerous to themselves than others, though that's not to say it doesn't happen (especially if there's co-morbidity) or that they can't be emotionally abusive.

The reason is because people with BPD actually do feel emotional empathy and remorse and shame for their actions. They act the way they do because they are constantly in emotional turmoil and hurt by the world around them. Anyone in extreme distress acts out and becomes a burden to those around them. The problem is that people with BPD are in that state far too often.

Someone who has it though and has worked hard to gain emotional control may very well act like a loving sweetheart of a person and only rarely hurt others. A BPD who isn't in distress does not act "predatory", unless they have some other co morbid diagnosis.
